A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CR-Net and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Content can be reliably matched across the related-work relocation and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CR-Net pre-training, activation-reconstruction, downstream fine-tuning, and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds first-layer and activation-quantization experiments, throughput measurements, and empirical pipeline-communication measurements.

M1.justification: Appendix E.2.4 adds a CR-Net variant using NF4 activation quantization with DoubleQuant. The core cross-layer residual architecture, full-rank first layer, learnable scaling factors, and recomputation algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain C4-en language-model pre-training, TinyShakespeare activation studies, and Wikitext-2/arXiv fine-tuning. The added quantization and throughput experiments change computational configurations and testing procedures within retained language-modeling coverage. The 13B results and longer-sequence experiments already appear in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Table 3 substantially expands the primary comparison set: VeLoRA and FLoRA are added at 60M/130M, and LORO at 60M through 1B. New Figure 3 panels compare CR-Net against full-rank training and LORO. Earlier comparators remain; the Learnable-ResFormer passage clarifies the existing adaptation rather than establishing its replacement.

E3.justification: New protocols cover 350M first-layer and quantization controls, 1B inference with microbatch size 64, and 7B throughput with batch size 512. Appendix G adds a 70B pipeline measurement on eight A800/NVLink GPUs using 256-token sequences. These extend evaluation settings without revising the established pre-training protocols.

E4.justification: v2 expands supplementary validation to previously untested questions: whether the first layer must remain full-rank (Table 6), whether four-bit activation quantization preserves performance (Table 13), and whether pipeline communication is practical empirically (Appendix G). Existing rank-allocation, scaling-factor, and residual-pattern ablations are retained.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence levels, or significance tests are added or revised. The small whiskers in the retained training-throughput plot remain without further statistical explanation.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are unchanged, but substantial new entries appear. LORO reports perplexities of 18.84/15.19 at 350M/1B, versus CR-Net's retained 18.95/15.22. New first-layer and quantization variants obtain 19.68 and 19.32, respectively, versus 18.95. Figure 3 adds CR-Net throughput of 116100 tokens/s for 1B inference and 6509 for 7B training. Appendix G reports 1.380 seconds communication time and 192.5 GB/s bandwidth under its new hardware settings.

T1.justification: The cosine-similarity assumption, stable-rank definition, Theorem 1 and proof, and complexity/communication derivations are retained across appendix renumbering. Activation-function terminology and equation numbering change, without a new theorem or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about low-rank activation differences, CR-Net's architecture, recomputation efficiency, and pre-training performance. Highlighting existing 13B results in Section 5 does not introduce a new core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds a stability explanation contrasting preserved high-rank signals with projection-based approaches. v2 interprets the first-layer ablation as supporting signal reconstruction, discusses quantization's memory/perplexity tradeoff, and interprets measured NVLink communication as supporting deployment efficiency. The conclusion's existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies NF4/DoubleQuant with block size 16, throughput hardware and batch settings, and torch.distributed.pipelining with ten layers per GPU. It also clarifies scaling-factor selection, the Learnable-ResFormer implementation, and which model scales use recomputation. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for QLoRA, VeLoRA, and low-rank Riemannian optimization (LORO), plus a brief quantization discussion. FLoRA was already cited in v1 but becomes a reported comparator. Most related-work content is retained and relocated to Appendix A.

P1.justification: Related work precedes preliminaries in v2, and several related-work paragraphs move into a new appendix. Local rewrites clarify stability, throughput evaluation, and the residual baseline; acknowledgments are added. Most prose and the overall method-to-analysis-to-experiments narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 expands into three panels, Figures 4–6 are resized into one row, and Table 3 gains comparator rows. Tables 6 and 13 display new experiments; Table 5 redisplays the 13B endpoint already in v1 Table 10. Other displays are retained with relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added comparators, first-layer ablation, quantization test, and measured pipeline communication make v2's empirical evidence more informative. Benefits are limited by unchanged uncertainty reporting and the different hardware/sequence settings used for empirical versus theoretical communication comparisons. Table 3 also introduces LORO results that warrant qualification of the retained broad superiority language, but the additional evidence provides a modest net quality improvement.
